_about: The dashboard To-Do feed. Refreshed at every Rule 8 checkpoint alongside the session handoff — this is the handoff distilled into plain language for the 📋 button on every tab. Split For Sam (curation / decisions only a human makes) and For Fable (engineering, the next session picks up).
_as_of: 2026-08-14 · SkyGate — the side menu is yours to rearrange, and the long-red test is finally green.
_status: The Admin tab is live and the COBI side menu is now something you drag rather than something we edit in code. Order, grouping, names, which sites show what, and a new "only show this to signed-in people" setting — all from one place, all saved for everyone the moment you press Save. Beside every menu item the tab prints what ACTUALLY protects the data behind it, because hiding a menu item protects nothing. Sierra's ten built-in rules — the ones that outrank the instructions you write — are visible and editable for the first time, on the Sierra Training tab. And the test that had been red on every commit for two days is green: 19 of its 26 flagged items turned out to be real governance gaps, including the workplan itself, which had no named owner.

items.text: Drag something, press Save, then reload the page. Everything here was tested against a simulated browser and nothing has been tried in a real one — we can't reach the site from here. If it goes wrong the worst case is the menu you already have, and the "Reset to how it ships" button puts everything back.

Six new decision rights need an owner (DR-13 to DR-18). Start with DR-13, the workplan itself — it is the most public thing we publish, four of its tables can be edited in-page by anyone with the team phrase, and until today nobody was named as its owner. DR-14 (who rotates the shared phrases, and when) is the second one worth naming.

Seven scheduled jobs run every week or month that nobody has listed as a cadence — landing pages, credential catalog, CPL News, stories, reflections, and two reference syncs. Each needs either an owner or a note saying it is just plumbing. This is the whole remaining backlog on that page now.

Scroll to "Sierra's built-in rules" and read them. These are the ten rules that OUTRANK the instructions you write above — one of them is why your 13:33 instruction on Wednesday didn't take effect. You can now edit any of them, and the four safety ones are marked so you can only add to them, never replace them.

Sierra named 1 of 9 AWS D1.1 credentials, and Riverside and Lemoore never appeared at all. Still not diagnosed: whether the search never found them, or the answer only printed the strongest match. That distinction decides the fix — measure first.

Build the "which rules were in play for this answer" view. Sierra already records it on every turn; nothing shows it. Being able to SEE the rule that fought your instruction is worth more than being able to edit it.

The two-lane memory tab — what we know (cpl_memory) beside what Sierra actually does (sierra_rules), linked by memory_slug — plus the check that reports "decided in memory, no Sierra rule implements it." Now unblocked, and it would have caught three separate misses this month.

The MAP Users section of our project notes has grown into a 4,400-character log and the lint has flagged it for five sessions running. Whoever next works on MAP Users has to compact it as part of that work — nobody else can safely tell which lines are still load-bearing.
